citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209.
creator: Johannes Welbl (University College London), Nelson F. Liu (University of Washington), Matt Gardner (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: SciQ is a dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced using a novel two-step method that leverages domain-specific textbooks and model-generated answer distractor suggestions. Each question includes a question, four answer options (one correct and three distractors), and an associated passage from a science textbook used to formulate the question. The dataset covers biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics topics spanning elementary to college introductory level.
name: SciQ
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was processed by at least two crowd workers: one for question formulation and one for distractor selection and quality validation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A qualitative evaluation was conducted: 100 original science exam questions and 100 SciQ training instances were presented to human judges who were asked to identify which was the real exam question. Judges identified the science exam question in 55% of cases, which falls below the significance level of p=0.05 under a null hypothesis of random guessing, indicating crowdsourced questions are indistinguishable from original exam questions. Additionally, 92.8% of questions passed the quality control check in the distractor selection task.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-step crowdsourcing process: (1) Question Formulation Task — workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs, chose one (or rejected all), and wrote a science exam question with a correct answer. Instructions specified: no yes/no questions, questions must not require further context, should query general principles rather than highly specific facts, question length 6–30 words, answer length up to 3 words, no ambiguous questions. Examples of desirable and undesirable questions were provided. (2) Distractor Selection Task — a second worker validated the (question, answer) pair (marking it as ungrammatical, having a false answer, unrelated to science, or requiring very specific background knowledge), then selected up to two of six model-suggested distractors and wrote at least one distractor themselves. Workers required AMT Master's status for both tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is intentionally domain-targeted to science exam topics (biology, chemistry, earth science, physics) at elementary to college introductory level. The base corpus was deliberately chosen to avoid overly specific facts (e.g., Simple Wikipedia was considered but rejected for being too specific). The method was designed to enforce diversity in question content and lexical expression by requiring workers to choose from multiple passage options. 36.1% of distractors in the final dataset were generated by the model rather than humans, which may introduce systematic patterns from the distractor model's training data (real 4th and 8th grade science exam questions).
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected via a two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. In the first step, crowd workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs, chose one, and wrote a question answerable from that passage along with a correct answer. In the second step, a different worker validated the question and selected or wrote three answer distractors, aided by model-generated distractor suggestions. A total of 175 workers participated. The total budget was $10,415. Workers required AMT Master's status; the first task paid $0.30 per HIT and the second $0.20 per HIT.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small percentage of passages were obtained from unreleasable texts and were excluded from the direct-answer version of SciQ, resulting in a smaller direct-answer dataset (10,481 train, 887 dev, 884 test) compared to the full multiple choice dataset (11,679 train, 1,000 dev, 1,000 test).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 science study textbooks from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics from elementary to college introductory level. CK-12 books were obtained under the Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial 3.0 Unported (CC BY-NC 3.0) License. A small percentage of passages came from unreleasable texts and were excluded from the direct-answer version of SciQ.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Document analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Neural models do not beat simple information retrieval baselines on the multiple choice version of SciQ, suggesting the dataset may not be sufficiently challenging for distinguishing neural from retrieval-based approaches. The direct-answer version is smaller than the multiple choice version due to unreleasable source texts. The dataset is limited to science domains covered by the 28 source textbooks. Multiword expression distractors were more likely to be unrelated or ungrammatical despite inclusion of part-of-speech features in the distractor model.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to individual paragraphs of the base corpus. Sentences were filtered out if they: (i) were a question or exclamation, (ii) had no verb phrase, (iii) contained modal verbs, (iv) contained imperative phrases, (v) contained demonstrative pronouns, (vi) contained personal pronouns other than third-person, (vii) began with a pronoun, (viii) contained first names, (ix) had fewer than 6 or more than 18 tokens or more than 2 commas, (x) contained special characters other than punctuation, (xi) had more than three tokens beginning uppercase, (xii) mentioned a graph, table or web link, (xiii) began with a discourse marker, (xiv) contained absolute wording (e.g., 'never', 'nothing', 'definitely'), or (xv) contained instructional vocabulary ('teacher', 'worksheet', etc.). A paragraph was accepted if a minimum number of sentences passed the filter. The dataset was randomly shuffled and split into train (11,679), validation (1,000), and test (1,000) portions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables progress on science exam question answering, a high-level NLP task requiring mastery of information extraction, reading comprehension, and common sense reasoning. It addresses the bottleneck of lacking large in-domain training sets for science QA, potentially enabling more sophisticated AI systems for educational applications.
rai:dataUseCases: Science exam question answering (both multiple choice and direct answer/reading comprehension settings); training data for neural models in medium-sized data settings; augmenting training data to improve performance on real 4th and 8th grade science exam questions; studying reading comprehension models where training examples number in the tens of thousands.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest classifier (trained on 3,705 real science exam questions) was used to rank and suggest answer distractors for crowd workers. Features included GloVe embeddings, POS-tag consistency indicators, WordNet-based hypernymy indicators, and OpenIE-based knowledge base links. The candidate distractor set contained 488,819 expressions including the 400K GloVe vocabulary items. A noisy classifier was also used to find relevant passages from the base corpus for presentation to workers.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper only states that 175 workers participated and that AMT Master's status was required; no demographic information (age, gender, nationality, language background) is provided.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific dates or time period for data collection are mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; the dataset consists of discrete QA items.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, balancing) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of science exam questions and passages; no personal or sensitive information is collected or described.
